title: AbbVie (ABBV) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript - Fortune
content:
OperatorGood morning, thank you for standing by. Welcome to the AbbVie Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be able to listen only until the question and answer portion of this call. You may ask a question by pressing star one on your phone. Today's call is also being recorded. If you have any objections, you may disconnect at this time. I would now like to introduce Ms. Liz Shea, Senior Vice President, Investor Relations. Liz SheaGood morning, thanks for joining us. Also on the call with me today are Rob Michael, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Jeff Stewart, Executive Vice President, Chief Commercial Officer, Roopal Thakkar, Executive Vice President, Research and Development, Chief Scientific Officer, and Scott Reents, Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer. Before we get started, I'll note that some statements we make today may be considered forward-looking statements based on our current expectations. AbbVie cautions that these forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from those indicated in our forward-looking statements. Additional information about these risks and uncertainties is included in our SEC filings. AbbVie undertakes no obligation to update these forward-looking statements except as required by law. On today's conference call, non-GAAP financial measures will be used to help investors understand AbbVie's business performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are reconciled with comparable GAAP financial measures in our earnings release and regulatory filings from today, which can be found on our website. Following our prepared remarks, we'll take your questions. With that, I'll turn the call over to Rob. Rob MichaelThank you, Liz. Good morning, everyone, thank you for joining us. AbbVie delivered another excellent quarter, with results once again exceeding our expectations. I'm especially pleased with the execution across our business, including double-digit sales growth from our diverse portfolio, the advancement of our compelling pipeline of innovative medicines, and our planned acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics, which represents an exciting opportunity to bolster AbbVie's leading immunology portfolio. Turning to our second quarter performance, we achieved adjusted earnings per share of $3.65, which is $0.06 above our guidance midpoint. Total net revenues were nearly $17 billion, beating our expectations by $300 million, and reflecting robust sales growth of 10.2%. The performance of SKYRIZI, RINVOQ, and our neuroscience portfolio continues to be very strong, with each delivering growth above 20%. Based on this momentum, we are raising our full-year revenue guidance by $300 million and have now raised total revenue by $600 million since the start of the year. Turning now to R&D, we continue to make excellent progress advancing our pipeline. Recent highlights from our late-stage programs include the U.S. approval of DECNUPAZ, a treatment for a rare form of blood cancer. This represents AbbVie's first marketed ADC in hematology. We also received European approvals for QULIPTA to treat acute migraine, TEPKINLY for second-line follicular lymphoma, as well as Boey, a first-in-class short-acting toxin in aesthetics. In addition, we received European approvals for RINVOQ in both vitiligo and alopecia areata, with U.S. regulatory decisions forthcoming. Based on the compelling data generated for each of these programs, we now anticipate the combined peak sales for these two indications alone to approach $2 billion, which is meaningfully above our prior expectations. During the quarter, we also announced the acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics, which will add multiple differentiated assets in dermatology, respiratory, and other related inflammatory diseases with significant sales potential. The acquisition will add even more depth to our robust pipeline in immunology, which we expect will be a major growth driver for AbbVie over the long term. This transaction is an excellent fit with our strategy to build and advance a compelling pipeline with new sources of growth to support AbbVie's performance in the 2030s and beyond. We have ample financial capacity for more business development and remain focused on adding both early and late-stage opportunities across our core disease areas. In summary, we are delivering outstanding execution across our business, and our long-term outlook remains very strong. With that, I'll turn the call over to Jeff for additional comments on our commercial highlights. Jeff? Jeff StewartThank you, Rob. I'll start with the quarterly results for immunology, which delivered total revenues of nearly $8.8 billion, reflecting very strong operational sales growth of 14.6%. SKYRIZI total sales were $5.5 billion, up 24% on an operational basis, once again exceeding our expectations. I'm very pleased with our performance in psoriasis, where we continue to capture robust in-play share of new and switching patients at a rate which is impressively four times higher than any other biologic or oral treatment in the U.S. We have achieved market share leadership now in more than 30 countries and see substantial room for continued growth globally. We do not expect a material impact to our robust outlook in psoriasis from existing or new therapies given SKYRIZI's very distinct profile. This includes high and very durable skin clearance from head to toe, widely demonstrated superior efficacy in head-to-head trials versus five different mechanisms, including both biologics and oral agents, simple and convenient quarterly dosing, and extremely strong long-term data in psoriatic arthritis extending now to five years, which is very important to prescribers as roughly 30% of psoriasis patients ultimately develop PsA. As well as now our recent approval for pediatric use with the new weight-based dosing option. In IBD, SKYRIZI's fastest-growing indication, we continue to capture a leading share of total new patient starts in the U.S. in the quarter, including substantial leadership in the front-line setting, the clearest signal of physician preference. Competitive dynamics remain in line with our expectations with the IL-23 category seeing very robust growth in both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. Importantly, we are also preparing for the potential approval of our subcutaneous induction dosing option for Crohn's later this fall, which is supported by very strong data, particularly in the front line, where we observe the highest levels of endoscopic response seen in the category. Turning now to RINVOQ, which is also performing above our expectations. Global sales were more than $2.5 billion, up 23.7% on an operational basis. I am especially pleased with the momentum we see in gastroenterology, where RINVOQ is on pace to deliver 30% global sales growth this year. RINVOQ has set a very high bar for efficacy in both ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, demonstrating strong rates of remission and endoscopic improvement. We continue to see a nice inflection of in-play patient share following the recently expanded label supporting access to RINVOQ earlier in the treatment paradigm for IBD patients. More broadly, we continue to see strong demand across all of RINVOQ indications. We are very excited about the growth potential in dermatology with vitiligo and alopecia areata now approved in Europe, with U.S. approval decisions anticipated over the next few quarters. RINVOQ's profile is competitively positioned for both of these chronic diseases, where our recently expanded U.S. derm field force will support both launches. Lastly, in immunology, HUMIRA global sales were $756 million, down 36.1% on an operational basis, reflecting biosimilar competition and in line with our expectations. Moving to neuroscience, where we once again outperformed our expectations. Total revenues were more than $3.2 billion, up approximately 20% on an operational basis. All three of our leading neuro pillars continue to demonstrate robust sales growth. In psychiatry, VRAYLAR global sales were nearly $1.1 billion, up approximately 19%, reflecting share gains in both bipolar disorder and adjunctive MDD. In migraine, our leading portfolio continues to deliver outstanding results, with BOTOX therapeutic, UBRELVY, and QULIPTA each delivering double-digit sales growth again this quarter. QULIPTA is now approved in Europe for adults as both an acute treatment option for migraine attacks and as a once-daily preventative treatment option for chronic or episodic migraine. The acute indication expansion in international markets for QULIPTA further supports our long-term outlook for our oral CGRPs to collectively achieve more than $5 billion of peak sales. Moving to Parkinson's disease, another substantial long-term growth driver for AbbVie. Total sales for VYALEV were $256 million, up more than 27% on a sequential basis. VYALEV is well on track to achieve blockbuster sales this year. We expect continued robust momentum in Parkinson's with the anticipated U.S. approval and launch of tavapadone in the third quarter. Feedback from key opinion leaders has been very positive, with tavapadone demonstrating strong efficacy as both a monotherapy as well as an add-on to standard of care. Overall, we believe our Parkinson's portfolio with VYALEV, tavapadone, and DUOPA will be a substantial commercial opportunity. We continue to expect collective Parkinson's peak sales of more than $5 billion. Turning now to oncology, where total revenues were more than $1.6 billion, down 2.4% on an operational basis. Total VENCLEXTA sales were $771 million, up 9.6% on an operational basis. Performance in CLL continues to be strong as VENCLEXTA use in combination with BTK inhibitors is expanding as a preferred fixed-duration treatment globally. Double-digit sales growth from ELAHERE, TEPKINLY, and EMRELIS also helped to partially offset the sales decline for IMBRUVICA, which was down 29.4% as expected due to IRA pricing and competitive share pressure. We also launched DECNUPAZ, a new therapeutic option for patients living with BPDCN, an ultra-rare form of blood cancer, further expanding AbbVie's emerging ADC portfolio. Moving now to aesthetics, which delivered global sales of nearly $1.3 billion, down 0.9% on an operational basis. BOTOX Cosmetic total revenues were $728 million, up 3.4% operationally, reflecting modest market growth globally. JUVÉDERM global sales were $245 million, down 6.6% operationally, reflecting continued headwinds in key dermal filler markets. As the industry leader, we continue to invest in this highly under-penetrated market to support long-term growth. I'm especially pleased with the recent Europe and Canada approvals of Boey, our fast-acting, short-duration toxin. Boey complements our toxin portfolio very nicely and represents a new way for patients to initiate an aesthetic treatment. We expect Boey will meaningfully expand the toxin market and look forward to potentially bringing this exciting innovation to the U.S. Overall, we continue to demonstrate outstanding commercial execution. With that, I'll turn the call over to Roopal  for comments on our R&D highlights. Roopal ? Roopal ThakkarThank you, Jeff. I'll begin with dermatology programs in immunology. RINVOQ was approved in Europe for the treatment of severe alopecia and non-segmental vitiligo. Applications are also under review in the U.S., with approval decisions anticipated later this year for vitiligo and early next year for alopecia areata. In hidradenitis suppurativa, we remain on track for 16-week data later this year from both RINVOQ and lutikizumab phase III trials. In our early-stage dermatology pipeline, three programs were recently advanced into the clinic, including an IL-13/IL-31 receptor bispecific antibody for atopic dermatitis, an oral IL-23 receptor inhibitor for psoriasis, and a long-acting IL-1 alpha/beta bispecific antibody for hidradenitis suppurativa. Turning to gastroenterology, the U.S. application for SKYRIZI subcutaneous induction in Crohn's disease is under review, with an approval decision expected later this fall. The subcutaneous regimen demonstrated very high levels of endoscopic response and clinical remission, with rates on both measures 25 points higher than placebo in the overall population and 45 points higher in patients who had not previously experienced advanced therapy. To our knowledge, these results in patients naive to advanced therapies are the highest reported for induction therapies in Crohn's disease, comparing very favorably to SKYRIZI IV and other approved agents. Full results from the study will be presented this fall, which will include additional important endpoints such as endoscopic remission. Startup activities are underway for our phase II-B combination trial in IBD. This multi-arm study will evaluate SKYRIZI plus a higher dose of our novel anti-alpha-4 beta-7 antibody and extended half-life TL1A antibody in both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. Interim results for SKYRIZI plus anti-alpha-4 beta-7 in Crohn's disease demonstrated a doubling of endoscopic remission at week 24 compared to either monotherapy. This study is expected to complete this fall, final results will be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting. Lastly, in immunology, we announced the planned acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics, which adds a portfolio of long-acting biologics targeting atopic dermatitis, respiratory conditions, and other immune-mediated diseases. These novel assets are highly complementary to our immunology strategy and further strengthen an already robust pipeline. Moving to neuroscience. QULIPTA was approved in Europe for the acute treatment of migraine, expanding options for patients. In Parkinson's disease, an FDA approval decision is expected in the third quarter for tavapadon. Results from three phase III trials demonstrated that this novel selective D1/D5 dopamine agonist has the potential to be a highly effective treatment for motor symptoms with low rates of dyskinesia, edema, sedation, and impulse control disorder. We look forward to bringing this innovation to patients later this year. In our early-stage neuroscience pipeline, multiple new trials were recently initiated, including a phase II study for a novel toxin, [Gemibotulinum], in essential tremor and a phase I-B study for ABBV-1758, a blood-brain barrier-crossing anti-pyroglutamate A-beta antibody in Alzheimer's disease. In schizophrenia, the multi-ascending dose study for emraclidine is nearing completion. The 100 mg dose retained a safe and tolerable profile, 150 mg is being evaluated. Dose selection for both schizophrenia and psychosis programs is expected in the coming months, we remain on track to begin phase II studies in the fourth quarter. Moving to solid tumor programs. Progress with Temab-A continues across a broad range of tumor types. In colorectal cancer, breakthrough therapy designation was granted for Temab-A in combination with bevacizumab in refractory metastatic CRC. This designation supports our phase III strategy in an all-comer third-line-plus setting, the trial is now actively recruiting. In second-line CRC, data are expected later this year from a phase II study evaluating Temab-A combinations versus chemotherapy. These results will help inform the development strategy for Temab-A in first and second-line CRC, as in irinotecan replacement. Early-stage results in ovarian and head and neck cancers were presented at the recent ASCO meeting, demonstrating Temab-A's potential in both tumor types. In platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, Temab-A showed strong anti-tumor activity, particularly in c-MET-selected patients, where response rates reached as high as 80%. Temab-A also demonstrated a 50% response rate in clear cell carcinoma, a segment with high unmet need that typically does not respond well to cytotoxic therapy. Plans to advance Temab-A in ovarian cancer will be discussed with regulators over the coming months. In c-MET-selected patients with advanced head and neck cancer, Temab-A demonstrated a 31% response rate and a median overall survival of 15.3 months, which compares favorably to standard of care. A phase II study evaluating Temab-A plus pembrolizumab in frontline will start soon. In pancreatic cancer, a phase II study evaluating Temab-A with FOLFOX as a frontline combination therapy was recently initiated. Turning to hematologic oncology, progress continues with etentamig across lines of therapy in multiple myeloma. An interim analysis is planned in the third quarter for progression-free survival from the monotherapy third-line-plus trial. If this interim analysis is positive, regulatory submission would occur later this year. A phase III study evaluating etentamig in combination with pomalidomide in second-line-plus patients, including those that were exposed or refractory to an anti-CD38 antibody or who lost response to an anti-BCMA CAR T or ADC will begin by year-end. Additionally, encouraging early-stage results for etentamig in relapse refractory light chain amyloidosis were presented at the recent EHA Congress. At the 40 mg dose, 100% of patients achieved hematologic complete response with a promising safety profile that included no CRS or ICANS. Based on these results, a phase III trial in newly diagnosed patients is being planned. Also in hematology, DECNUPAZ received FDA approval for blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm, an ultra-rare and aggressive blood cancer. As a new treatment alternative providing durable responses with a manageable safety profile and outpatient administration, DECNUPAZ offers a meaningful benefit to patients with this rare cancer. Moving to aesthetics, our rapid onset and short duration toxin, Boey, was approved in Europe and Canada for the temporary improvement in appearance of glabellar lines. This marks an important milestone in aesthetic medicine. Boey was developed to allow patients to temporarily preview the benefits of cosmetic toxins without worrying about long-lasting results. Clinicians and patients now have another option to tailor treatment to individual needs and goals. In summary, we are making meaningful progress with our pipeline and look forward to additional important data readouts, regulatory submissions, and approvals throughout the remainder of 2026. With that, I'll turn the call over to Scott. Scott ReentsThank you, Roopal . Starting with our second quarter results, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.65, which is $0.06 above our guidance midpoint. These results include a $0.17 unfavorable impact from acquired IPR&D expense. Quarterly net revenues were nearly $17 billion, reflecting robust growth of 10.2%, including a 0.7% favorable impact from foreign exchange. Adjusted gross margin was 84.7% of sales. Adjusted R&D expense was 13.6% of sales, and adjusted SG&A expense was 21% of sales. The adjusted operating margin was 48.3% of sales, which includes a 1.7% unfavorable impact from acquired IPR&D expense. Net interest expense was $679 million. The adjusted tax rate was 14.7%. Turning to our financial outlook, we are updating our full-year adjusted earnings per share guidance to between $13.87 and $14.07. This update reflects a $0.10 improvement in the outlook of our existing business based on strong second quarter results and continued momentum. It also now includes $0.14 of anticipated dilution related to the planned Apogee acquisition that is more than offsetting our underlying over-performance. We continue to expect that the Apogee transaction will close in the third quarter. This guidance does not include an estimate for acquired IPR&D expense that may be incurred beyond the second quarter. We now expect total net revenues of approximately $67.6 billion, an increase of $300 million. This assumes a roughly 0.5% favorable impact from foreign exchange on full-year sales growth, reflecting less benefit than our previous expectation. Our increased revenue forecast includes the following approximate assumptions for several of our key products and therapeutic areas. We now expect SKYRIZI global revenues of $21.7 billion, an increase of $100 million based on momentum across psoriatic and IBD indications. Total neuroscience revenues of $12.7 billion, an increase of $100 million, now reflecting VRAYLAR sales approaching $4.1 billion and BOTOX therapeutic sales approaching $4.2 billion. The remaining $100 million increase reflects momentum from RINVOQ and VENCLEXTA. Moving to the P&L for 2026, we continue to forecast full year adjusted gross margin above 84% of sales. We now expect adjusted R&D expense of approximately $9.8 billion, an increase of $100 million reflecting Apogee-related pipeline investments.                                        My Trusted Source The transaction adds a late-stage immunology pipeline to a company already known for its leading position in that field, and it arrives as the company approaches its latest-quarter earnings report. For followers of dividend-paying healthcare names, AbbVie is a familiar story. The company was created through a separation from Abbott Laboratories, built its fortunes on the immunology medicine Humira and has since worked to replace that franchise with newer products such as Skyrizi and Rinvoq while expanding in neuroscience and aesthetics. In a press release furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission, AbbVie announced that it had completed its acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics. The announcement ended a process that began when AbbVie disclosed its agreement to acquire the biotechnology company, which had been developing next-generation antibody medicines for inflammatory diseases. Closing the deal means that the acquired programmes now sit inside AbbVie's research organisation and that their costs and any eventual revenues will flow into AbbVie's financial statements. The release also contained a reaffirmation of guidance for the full year and for the latest quarter, which is a common feature when a company completes a sizeable transaction: it tells the market that the acquisition's financial effect has been built into the numbers management had already described. Beyond that, Apogee has a combination programme that pairs zumilokibart with a long-acting antibody against thymic stromal lymphopoietin, another protein linked to airway and skin inflammation. Additional antibodies in the portfolio address atopic dermatitis, asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. All of these remain in development and none has been approved by regulators. AbbVie was candid that the acquisition will dilute adjusted earnings per share in the near term. The release states that dilution is expected this year and by a larger amount the following year, with the transaction not expected to start adding to adjusted earnings per share until several years later, at the start of the next decade. The reason is straightforward. Apogee's medicines are still in clinical development, so they generate no sales, yet AbbVie takes on the associated research costs and the financing cost of paying for the deal. Meanwhile, accounting rules for asset acquisitions mean that the upfront price may be expensed as acquired research and development, which depresses adjusted earnings in the period it is recorded. Readers following Dividend Stocks can place this update within its wider category. Immunology has been AbbVie's core for over a decade. The company's response has been to build successors, chiefly Skyrizi for psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease and Rinvoq for several immune-mediated conditions, so that the immunology franchise can continue to grow even as Humira declines. The pitch for the new programmes is convenience: less frequent injections could matter to patients and physicians if clinical data prove durable in larger trials. The press release on the acquisition does not discuss Skyrizi or Rinvoq sales, so those figures will become available only in the full latest-quarter report. Readers wanting that detail should wait for the earnings release and the associated quarterly filing. Beyond immunology, AbbVie operates in several other areas. Its neuroscience unit includes medicines for migraine, Parkinson's disease and psychiatric conditions, and the company has expanded in that field through acquisitions. Its oncology franchise includes blood-cancer treatments, and its aesthetics business, built around the Botox brand and the Allergan product range, supplies cosmetic and facial treatments directly to physicians and consumers. The aesthetics business is sensitive to consumer spending because most procedures are paid for out of pocket. Neuroscience, by contrast, depends more on reimbursement and the adoption of newer medicines. AbbVie has been an active acquirer. Its acquisition of Allergan transformed the business by adding aesthetics, eye care and neuroscience, and it has subsequently completed a string of smaller transactions to add clinical-stage assets. The Apogee deal fits a pattern in which the company seeks to supplement its internal research with externally discovered programmes at a fairly advanced stage. This approach has advantages and drawbacks. Acquiring a late-stage asset shortens the time to possible approval and reduces some scientific uncertainty, but it typically requires a high price because competitors also want such assets. title: Buy, Hold or Sell ABBV Stock? Key Tips Ahead of Q3 Earnings - The Globe and Mail
content: AbbVie ABBV is set to report third-quarter 2026 earnings on Oct. 30, before the opening bell. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the to-be-reported quarter’s sales is pinned at $17.37 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) are estimated at $3.77. Both metrics indicate an increase from the year-ago period. Over the past 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 EPS has declined from $14.05 to $13.95, while the 2027 estimate has fallen from $16.15 to $16.05. The near-term decline is primarily attributed to the impact of acquired IPR&D and milestone expenses totaling $216 million, which the company expects to have been recorded in the quarter, as noted in an SEC filing released earlier this month. AbbVie’s performance has been impressive, with its earnings exceeding expectations in each of the trailing four quarters. It has delivered a trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise of 2.10%. In the last reported quarter, the pharma giant delivered an earnings surprise of 0.27%. Per our proven model, companies with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) have a good chance of delivering an earnings beat. This is not the case here. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they’re reported with our Earnings ESP Filter. AbbVie currently has an Earnings ESP of -0.33% and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here. For the third quarter of 2026, AbbVie expects adjusted earnings to be in the range of $3.73-$3.77 per share. The company expects net revenues of approximately $17.2 billion. Currency is expected to have an unfavorable impact of around 0.4% on sales. AbbVie’s top-line growth in the third quarter is likely to have been driven by higher sales of immunology drugs Skyrizi and Rinvoq. Strong volume growth and market share gains across approved indications have been driving sales of both drugs. During the third quarter, Rinvoq’s label was expanded in the EU across three indications — vitiligo, alopecia areata and active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis. This expansion might have further boosted sales in the third quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Skyrizi sales is pegged at $5.72 billion, while the same for Rinvoq is pinned at $2.73 billion. Sales of the company’s flagship drug Humira are likely to have continued their downward trend due to biosimilar erosion. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the drug’s sales is pegged at $695 million. Within AbbVie’s oncology franchise, sales of J&JJNJ-partnered Imbruvica are expected to continue their downward trajectory, reflecting intensifying competition from newer oral therapies. The decline is likely to have accelerated in the to-be-reported quarter, as IRA-driven pricing changes that took effect at the beginning of the year are expected to have put additional pressure on sales. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Imbruvica sales is pegged at approximately $530 million. In contrast, sales of Roche RHHBY-partnered Venclexta are expected to have risen during the to-be-reported quarter, driven by sustained demand in the chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), particularly due to its use in combination with BTK inhibitors. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Venclexta sales is pegged at $793 million. Overall, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for oncology revenues is pegged at $1.68 billion, indicating relatively flat year over year. While the anticipated weakness in Imbruvica sales is expected to weigh on the franchise’s performance, growth in Venclexta and contributions from AbbVie’s newer oncology products are likely to offset this pressure. AbbVie’s neuroscience franchise has delivered strong growth in recent quarters, a trend that is expected to have continued in the to-be-reported quarter. Growth is likely to have been driven by higher sales of Botox Therapeutic, the depression drug Vraylar and the migraine treatments — Ubrelvy and Qulipta. The Parkinson’s disease drug Vyalev is also expected to have contributed to the franchise’s performance during the quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for neuroscience product sales is pinned at approximately $3.29 billion. In the aesthetics franchise, sales are expected to have shown signs of recovery following sluggish performance in recent quarters, primarily due to softness in Botox Cosmetic and Juvederm filler sales. The anticipated improvement is likely to have been supported by stabilizing demand in the U.S. facial injectable market and easing macroeconomic pressures, which may have helped improve consumer sentiment. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for aesthetics product sales is pegged at $1.20 billion, indicating relatively flat year-over-year. Nonetheless, a single quarter’s results are not so important for long-term investors. Let us delve deeper to understand whether to buy, sell or hold the stock at present. Year to date, shares of the company have risen 25.5% compared with the industry’s 17.2% growth. From a valuation standpoint, AbbVie is trading at a discount to the industry. Based on the price/earnings (P/E) ratio, the shares currently trade at 18.29 times forward earnings, lower than the industry’s 19.02 times. Yet, compared to some of its peers like Pfizer PFE and Sanofi, the stock is trading at a premium. AbbVie has navigated Humira’s biosimilar erosion relatively well, with Skyrizi and Rinvoq emerging as its primary growth drivers. Strong demand, market-share gains and label expansions across existing and newer indications have helped the company offset declining Humira sales and strengthen its position in the immunology market. However, competition is intensifying, with J&J’s newly approved oral immunology drug Icotyde potentially posing a longer-term threat to Skyrizi if its use expands into additional indications. The growing neuroscience franchise, driven by Botox Therapeutic, Vraylar and migraine drugs, along with an expanding oncology portfolio, also supports its long-term growth prospects. However, declining Imbruvica sales amid intensifying competition and continued weakness in the aesthetics business remain key headwinds. Meanwhile, AbbVie’s aggressive business development strategy is strengthening its long-term growth prospects but weighing on near-term earnings. The company recently completed its $10.9 billion acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics, further expanding its immunology pipeline. However, the deal is expected to have diluted adjusted EPS by 14 cents in 2026 and approximately 46 cents in 2027, with accretion anticipated beginning in 2032. Additionally, $216 million in acquired IPR&D and milestone expenses is expected to have reduced third-quarter adjusted EPS by $0.11. These costs have contributed to downward revisions in earnings estimates, adding to near-term profitability concerns. While AbbVie’s core growth drivers and pipeline investments support its longer-term outlook, elevated expenses, declining near-term earnings estimates and intensifying competition warrant caution. The company must demonstrate that its investments can translate into sustainable earnings growth to restore near-term investor confidence. Given AbbVie’s Zacks Rank #4, negative Earnings ESP and recent downward revisions in earnings estimates, short-term investors may consider exiting ABBV stock, as near-term earnings uncertainty could limit further upside. However, long-term investors may choose to stay invested, as continued growth in Skyrizi, Rinvoq and other key therapies, along with an expanding pipeline, supports the company’s long-term growth prospects.  has confirmed that the company will host its third-quarter earnings conference call on Friday morning, with a live webcast opening before the American trading session begins. The announcement, circulated by the company and carried across financial news channels, places one of the largest names in branded pharmaceuticals squarely inside the busiest stretch of the reporting calendar. The stock remains one of the more closely followed names among Healthcare Stocks. The timing matters because late October has become the moment when most large drugmakers release quarterly figures within days of one another. Market participants tracking the sector now have a fixed date to anchor expectations, and the webcast will be accessible through the company website with an archived recording posted the same day. Because the figures land during peak pharmaceutical earnings season, the market reaction tends to be read in the context of what rival drugmakers report around the same dates. That clustering gives each individual print added weight, and the end-of-week slot means the numbers will set the tone heading into the following week. The company has framed the quarter as another step in a multi-year transition, and the end-of-week timing ensures the figures arrive while the broader drug group is still reporting. Attention centres on how the company has managed the transition away from its best-known legacy immunology product, whose exclusivity lapsed and opened the door to lower-cost rivals. Two newer immunology therapies have been positioned as the engines meant to absorb that erosion, and the quarterly print is widely regarded as a check on how quickly that handover is progressing. Beyond the headline revenue lines, market observers will be reading the commentary for colour on demand across immunology, aesthetics and the newer neuroscience and oncology assets. Each segment carries its own dynamics, and the combined picture tends to shape how the broader branded-pharma group trades in the days that follow. The company has also drawn attention for the pace at which it has reshaped its revenue mix since the legacy franchise began to decline. Demonstrating that the successor brands can keep compounding, while the aesthetics and newer pipeline assets contribute, is the running narrative the market expects the report to advance. Each successive report has shown the revenue mix tilting further toward the successor brands, and the market expects the coming print to extend that trend. Immunology sits at the heart of the AbbVie model. The company built a global franchise around treatments for chronic inflammatory conditions spanning rheumatology, dermatology and gastroenterology, and that base generated the scale that funded expansion into other areas. The strategic question that keeps recurring is whether the two successor therapies can grow fast enough, across enough indications, to more than replace the mature product they were designed to follow. Demand trends for those two brands have therefore become the single most watched metric whenever the company reports, and the coming call will add a fresh data point to that running story. Both successor brands have been expanding into additional approved uses, each new indication widening the pool of patients they can reach. That breadth is central to the design of the franchise, because a therapy approved across many conditions can keep growing even as competition intensifies in any single one. The scale built by the immunology base gives the company flexibility to fund research and acquisitions that smaller peers cannot match, a structural trait the market keeps in view. For much of the past decade the business leaned on a single immunology therapy that became one of the best-selling medicines in the world. Once American exclusivity ended, a wave of competing biosimilars arrived and pricing pressure followed, steadily compressing the contribution from that franchise. Management framed this transition years in advance, and the market has largely absorbed the idea that the legacy brand would decline. What remains genuinely uncertain is the slope of that decline and the pace at which the replacement portfolio fills the gap, which is exactly why each quarterly update carries weight. The erosion of a mega-blockbuster is a pattern seen across branded pharmaceuticals, yet few products reached the scale of this one, which magnifies the consequences of the handover. Each report offers a fresh reading on whether the newer portfolio is advancing faster than the legacy line is fading. The speed of the decline has moderated as biosimilar pricing stabilised, yet the franchise remains large enough that its trajectory still shapes the overall growth picture. The acquisition of a major aesthetics group brought a well-known wrinkle treatment and a family of dermal fillers into the fold, giving the company a consumer-facing medical-aesthetics arm that behaves differently from its prescription business. That segment is more sensitive to discretionary spending and broader consumer sentiment across American and international markets. Softer demand for elective aesthetic procedures has periodically weighed on the segment, and the quarterly commentary is often parsed for signs of a recovery or further softness. The division nonetheless gives the company exposure to a growth area outside traditional therapeutics. Because aesthetic procedures are frequently paid for out of pocket, the segment tracks consumer confidence more closely than prescription medicines do. That makes it a useful barometer of discretionary health spending and a distinct contributor to the overall revenue mix. International demand for aesthetic treatments has grown alongside the American market, giving the segment a global dimension that broadens its reach beyond any single economy. Alongside immunology and aesthetics, the company has been building neuroscience and oncology franchises intended to broaden the revenue base over the period ahead. Neuroscience spans treatments for psychiatric and neurological conditions, while the oncology arm has grown through both internal programs and acquisitions that added antibody-drug conjugate technology. These segments are smaller today than immunology, yet they represent the diversification the company has pursued to reduce dependence on any single therapy area. Progress across these pillars is a recurring theme on earnings calls and in pipeline updates. The neuroscience franchise has drawn attention for its migraine and psychiatric treatments, while oncology has leaned on blood-cancer therapies and newer targeted approaches. Growth across both areas is meant to steady the company as the immunology transition plays out. Bolt-on acquisitions have been a favoured way to add assets in these areas, and how those purchases mature is a recurring thread in company updates. The call arrives while the wider group of Healthcare Stocks is working through a dense run of quarterly reports, pricing debates and pipeline milestones. Large-cap branded pharmaceutical names, as members of the S&P 500, tend to move in loose sympathy during earnings season as each print reshapes expectations for the others. Defensive demand characteristics have long made healthcare a relatively steady corner of the market, yet the branded-drug subsector carries its own cycle tied to patent timelines, launch trajectories and regulatory developments. The AbbVie report feeds directly into that shared narrative. Within that landscape, the market treats the heaviest-weighted names as bellwethers whose results colour sentiment toward smaller peers. The stock also features in the NYSE Composite and the Russell 1000, which keeps its moves on the radar of index-linked funds. A clear print from a company of this size can set expectations for the entire branded-pharma cohort reporting in the same window. Macro conditions such as interest-rate shifts can also influence how the defensive healthcare segment trades relative to more cyclical corners of the market. Drug pricing remains a persistent theme across the American healthcare conversation, with government programs negotiating prices for selected high-spend medicines and ongoing debate about affordability. Branded manufacturers must navigate that environment while funding the research that supports new launches. Commentary on pricing pressure, access and the evolving reimbursement framework often features in quarterly discussions, and market participants listen closely for any shift in tone. The regulatory backdrop is a structural feature of the business rather than a one-off event, shaping planning across the entire group. Because several of the company franchises fall within the categories most affected by price negotiation, any update on how those discussions are unfolding can influence expectations for the segments involved. That makes the regulatory commentary a closely followed part of each report. Because the rules governing price negotiation continue to evolve, the company commentary on how it is adapting draws particular attention each quarter. AbbVie has built a reputation as a steady dividend payer, a trait that has drawn distribution-focused holders toward the stock over the years. A consistent distribution history is one reason the name features prominently in many large-cap healthcare baskets. Sustaining that distribution while funding research, servicing debt from past acquisitions and absorbing the legacy-product decline is part of the balancing act that management describes each quarter. The durability of cash generation is therefore a frequent point of discussion around the results. The payout record also reflects the company roots, since the business was spun out of a long-established healthcare parent with its own dividend heritage. Preserving that continuity through the immunology transition is a point the market watches each period. Beyond the marketed portfolio, the company maintains a broad pipeline spanning immunology, oncology, neuroscience and eye care. Late-stage readouts, regulatory submissions and label expansions for existing brands all factor into how the business is expected to evolve. Each quarterly update typically includes a pipeline progress section, and market observers weigh those milestones alongside the financial figures. New indications for the successor immunology therapies are a particular area of focus, since broader approvals widen the addressable patient base. The company has also used acquisitions to refill its pipeline, bringing in neuroscience and oncology assets that complement internal programs. How those acquired candidates progress through development is part of the longer growth story the market tracks. Several late-stage readouts expected over the coming periods could broaden the reach of the successor brands, and the market tracks those milestones closely. The clearest headwind remains biosimilar competition against the legacy franchise, which continues to pressure revenue from that product line. Elective-demand softness in aesthetics and the general uncertainty around drug pricing add further layers of complexity. Integration costs and debt associated with large acquisitions are also part of the picture, as the company works to turn those deals into durable revenue streams. None of these headwinds is new, yet together they frame the backdrop against which the quarterly performance will be judged. Currency swings across the company sizable international footprint can also move reported figures, adding another variable the market weighs when interpreting the quarter. Managing these overlapping pressures while sustaining research spending is the central task management describes. The company has nonetheless navigated prior patent transitions, and that track record informs how the market weighs the current set of headwinds. Immunology is one of the most fiercely contested arenas in medicine, with several large manufacturers fielding competing therapies for overlapping conditions. The arrival of biosimilars has intensified that competition and reshaped pricing across the category. In aesthetics, oncology and neuroscience the company faces a different set of rivals in each field. The breadth of that competition is one reason diversification has been central to the strategy, spreading exposure across multiple therapeutic battlegrounds rather than concentrating it in one. Newer classes of oral and injectable immunology treatments continue to enter the market, keeping competitive intensity high. The company response has been to broaden the approved uses of its successor brands faster than rivals can contest each one. Because AbbVie ranks among the heaviest-weighted healthcare names, the quarterly print tends to influence sentiment across the branded-pharma group and the broader defensive segment. A clear read on the immunology handover can move expectations for peers wrestling with their own patent timelines. The report also lands amid a packed week of healthcare results, so the market reaction will be read in the context of what rival drugmakers deliver around the same dates. That clustering amplifies the signal value of any single print. For holders of broad market and sector baskets, a company of this scale contributes meaningfully to how the healthcare slice performs. That gives the report relevance well beyond the company own stock. A clear print from a company of this weight can set the tone for the healthcare slice of major benchmarks during the reporting week. Ahead of the webcast, the central questions revolve around the growth pace of the two successor immunology brands, the trajectory of aesthetics demand and the cadence of pipeline progress. Guidance commentary, when offered, tends to carry as much weight as the reported quarter itself. With the call set for Friday morning, the company will soon add fresh detail to a story the market has followed closely for years. Until then, expectations remain anchored to the transition narrative that has defined the business through its post-exclusivity chapter. Market observers will also weigh any update on capital allocation, research priorities and how management characterises the balance between the fading legacy line and the growing successor portfolio. Those themes tend to shape sentiment as much as the headline numbers. Commentary on how management characterises demand across each segment will be weighed alongside the headline figures, since tone often matters as much as the numbers themselves.
